title: How many teams?
prompt:
In a league every team plays every other team exactly once. In total 91 games are played.

How many teams are in the league?
hints: If there are n teams, in how many games does each team take part, and why does multiplying by n count every one of the games twice?
So what must n × (n − 1) equal, in terms of the total number of games?
Which two consecutive whole numbers multiply to that?
solution:
**14.**

If there are n teams, each of the n takes part in n − 1 of the games, and n × (n − 1) counts every one of the games twice, once for each of its two sides. So n × (n − 1) ÷ 2 = 91, which means n × (n − 1) = 182. We need two consecutive whole numbers whose product is 182: 14 and 13, since 14 × 13 = 182. So there are **14** teams.

Check: 13 × 12 = 156 is too small and 15 × 14 = 210 is too big.

The common slip is solving n × (n − 1) = 91, without the doubling. The total was already halved.
